summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent ships a remote-controlled agent granting a WebSocket peer full PTY shell and self-update on the installer host
details: The package's main entrypoint opens a WebSocket to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via --server to a remote host) and dispatches server-sent message types to privileged local operations. `terminal_create` spawns bash/PowerShell via node-pty; `terminal_input` writes attacker-supplied bytes from msg.data directly into that PTY, giving the WebSocket peer arbitrary shell execution on the installer host. Additional message types perform arbitrary filesystem read/write and git operations. An `upgrade_agent` message triggers `npm view @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest version` followed by a detached upgrade.sh that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restarts the process via systemd/launchd/PM2, so any future compromise of the npm package propagates to all deployed agents on the next server-issued upgrade. service/linux.js additionally mutates PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of install-time environment setup. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket server has full remote command execution, file access, and self-update control over any host running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
